{{Top|ga}} {{Youmay|the Imperial officer|the astronomical object [[Corsin]]}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:Shaef_Corssin.png]] |name=Shaef Corssin |homeworld= |birth= |death= |species=[[Human]]''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' |gender= |pronouns=He/him[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] |height= |mass= |hair=[[Color|Blond]] |feathers= |eyes=Gray |skin=Light |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]]''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' **[[Imperial Navy's officer corps]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|The rebel flagship is disabled, my lord… but has received transmissions from the surface.|Captain Shaef Corssin to Darth Vader|audio=Corssin-Flagship.flac|}} The [[human]] '''Shaef Corssin''' was a competent and focused [[Imperial officer|officer]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Navy]]. He served as the [[captain]] of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Devastator]]'', [[flagship]] of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. In [[1 BBY]], the ''Devastator'' arrived [[Scarif system|above]] the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] as [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Rebel Alliance Navy|forces]] were attempting to [[Battle of Scarif|escape]] with the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. Corssin informed Vader once the ''Devastator'' had disabled the enemy [[Profundity|flagship]], and the [[Sith Lord]] ordered him to prepare a boarding party; however, a portion of the rebels eventually escaped with the [[Death Star]] plans. ==Biography== ===The Battle of Scarif=== {{Quote|Prepare a boarding party.''"
"''Yes, my lord.|Darth Vader and Shaef Corssin|audio=Vader-Corssin.flac|}} [[File:Devastator-GR75Destruction.png|thumb|left|300px|Under Corssin's command, the ''Devastator'' arrived at Scarif.]] Shaef Corssin was a [[human]] member of the [[Imperial Navy's officer corps]] during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. He served as [[captain]] of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Devastator]]'', [[flagship]] of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. In [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' to [[1 BBY]]. the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Battle of Scarif|attacked]] the Imperial forces stationed at [[Citadel Tower]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] in order to steal the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. Once the plans had been transmitted to the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] engaging the [[Imperial Navy|Imperial forces]] in [[orbit]], [[Admiral]] [[Raddus]] gave the order to retreat by jumping to [[hyperspace]]. As the ships began to jump, the ''Devastator'' arrived from hyperspace [[Scarif system|above Scarif]], causing several smaller Alliance vessels to collide with the [[Star Destroyer]] and break apart on its hull. The Imperial vessel then opened fire upon Raddus' ship, the [[MC75 Star Cruiser]] ''[[Profundity]]'', and managed to disable it, preventing it from fleeing. Corssin approached Vader upon the ''Devastator's'' [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] to let him know the enemy flagship was crippled, but also informed him about the transmission it had received. [[File:Corssin-Vader.png|thumb|right|300px|Shaef Corssin commanded the flagship of Darth Vader.]] The [[Sith Lord]] ordered Corssin to prepare a boarding party and left the bridge, joining the team to try and recover the [[Death Star]] plans; however, a small number of the rebels ultimately managed to escape with the plans aboard the [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]''.''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' The ''Devastator'' then gave chase after the [[corvette]], before ultimately [[Secret mission to Tatooine|capturing]] it above the planet [[Tatooine]] and then returning to the Death Star.{{Film|IV}} ===Post Scarif=== {{Quote|To support this argument, supporters of the "firepower" lobby highlighted how Vader's ship had no issues with disabling Raddus' flagship upon arriving at the battle, and ascribed much of this to both Vader's natural aggression and also Captain Shaef Corssin's greater military skill.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|}} [[File:Admiral_Gorin.png|thumb|left|250px|Corssin was considered to have greater military skill than Gorin.]] In the [[Standard day|days]] and [[Standard week|weeks]] following the Imperial failures at Scarif, there was contentious debate within the [[Imperial Military]] over how much blame lay with Admiral [[Gorin]], commander of the [[Scarif fleet]]. Those who did blame Gorin pointed to Corssin and Vader's success in disabling the ''Profundity'' where the admiral had failed as proof.''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' Corssin was no longer in command of the ''Devastator'' by the [[time]] of the [[Battle of Endor]]{{InsiderCite|issue1=149|issue2=150|Blade Squadron (short story)}} in [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' during which it was captained by Admiral [[Jhared Montferrat]]. In [[35 ABY]],{{RiseAndFallDate}} the [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] mentioned Corssin while covering the debate over Gorin in his''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''. ==Personality and traits== Corssin was a competent and fiercely focused [[Imperial officer]], speaking crisply when he addressed Vader on the ''Devastator's'' bridge. He had light skin, gray [[eye]]s, and blond [[hair]]. ==Skills and abilities== Members of the Imperial Military who believed Gorin was to blame for the failures at Scarif claimed Corssin possessed greater military skill then the admiral. ==Equipment== During the Battle of Scarif, Corssin wore black [[glove]]s and a standard gray [[Imperial officer's uniform]] that included a [[Imperial kepi|cap]], an [[officer's disk]], and another disk on the buckle of his black [[belt]]. On his [[breast]], he wore three [[code cylinder]]s alongside a [[rank insignia plaque]] that showed three blue squares and two red. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Corssin-GraphicNovel.png|thumb|right|300px|Shaef Corssin was given abbreviated dialogue and depicted with gray hair in ''Star Wars: Rogue One Graphic Novel Adaptation''.]] Shaef Corssin first appeared simultaneously in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', and [[Alexander Freed]]'s [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|novelization]] of the film released alongside it. Corssin was portrayed by [[Michael Shaeffer]] in the film and credited as "[[General]] Corssin," receiving the first name of Shaef, based on part of the actor's surname, in the accompanying reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]. The reference book also identified the character as a captain rather than a general. As Corssin is shown in ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' to be a naval officer, this article assumes that his correct rank is captain. The [[2017]] [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Graphic Novel Adaptation|graphic novel adaptation]] of ''Rogue One'' written by [[Alessandro Ferrari]] slightly abbreviates Corssin's dialogue and erroneously depicts him with gray hair.[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Graphic Novel Adaptation|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' Graphic Novel Adaptation]] An [[Unidentified Imperial captain (Devastator)|unnamed captain]] of the ''Devastator'' who is described as an older individual appears in ''[[A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy]]'', a [[2015]] novelization
